facts.fact: UPS is an option under the NPS for Central Government employees
facts.quote: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) is a pension scheme introduced by the Government of India, effective 1st April 2025, as an option under the National Pension System (NPS) for Central Government employees.

facts.fact: UPS took effect on 1 April 2025
facts.quote: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) is a pension scheme introduced by the Government of India, effective 1st April 2025

facts.fact: UPS was notified by the Ministry of Finance vide F. No. FX-1/3/2024-PR dated 24.01.2025
facts.quote: The Ministry of Finance, Government of India, had notified the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for eligible Central Government employees vide Notification F. No. FX-1/3/2024-PR dated 24.01.2025.

facts.fact: UPS operates within the NPS architecture regulated by PFRDA
facts.quote: UPS operates within the existing NPS architecture regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)

facts.fact: The CCS (Implementation of UPS under NPS) Rules, 2025 were notified on 02.09.2025
facts.quote: The Central Civil Services (Implementation of the Unified Pension Scheme under the National Pension System) Rules, 2025 have been notified on 02.09.2025 by the Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare

facts.fact: Employee contribution is 10% of Basic Pay + DA
facts.quote: Employee Contribution: 10% of Basic Pay + Dearness Allowance (DA).

facts.fact: Government makes a matching 10% contribution
facts.quote: Government Contribution: Matching 10% (from payroll system).

facts.fact: Government adds about 8.5% of Basic Pay + DA to a pool corpus
facts.quote: Additional Government Contribution: An estimated 8.5% of Basic Pay + DA to a Pool Corpus.

facts.fact: Assured payout is 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months, after at least 25 years of qualifying service
facts.quote: Assured Payout , at the rate of 50% of last 12 monthly average basic pay, immediately prior to superannuation. Assured payout is payable after a minimum 25 years of qualifying service.

facts.fact: The payout is proportionate for 10 to 25 years of service
facts.quote: Proportionate payout: Between 10 and 25 years of service.

facts.fact: Minimum payout is Rs 10,000 a month after at least 10 years of service
facts.quote: Minimum Guaranteed Payout: ₹10,000/month (after 10 years of service).

facts.fact: Family payout is 60% of the payout, to the legally wedded spouse
facts.quote: Family Payout: The legally wedded spouse shall receive 60% of admissible payout drawn by the subscriber immediately prior to the demise.

facts.fact: Dearness Relief is paid on both the payout and the family payout
facts.quote: Dearness Relief: Payable on both admissible payout and family payout, as notified by the Government.

facts.fact: Lump sum: 1/10 of (last Basic Pay + DA) for every completed 6 months of qualifying service
facts.quote: Lump Sum Payment: ₹ (1/10) × (Last Drawn Basic Pay + DA) for every completed 6 months of qualifying service.

facts.fact: Gratuity (retirement and death gratuity) is also given to UPS subscribers
facts.quote: Gratuity Benefits: Retirement Gratuity and Death Gratuity are extended to UPS subscribers under the CCS (Payment of Gratuity under NPS) Rules, 2021.

facts.fact: Final withdrawal of up to 60% of the corpus (individual or benchmark corpus, whichever is lower) reduces the payout proportionately
facts.quote: Final Withdrawal: Up to 60% of IC or BC, whichever is lower. Reduces assured payout proportionately.

facts.fact: Eligible: Central Government employees under NPS in service on 01.04.2025, and new recruits joining on or after 01.04.2025
facts.quote: UPS is available to: Existing Central Government Employees under NPS as on 01.04.2025. New Recruits joining Central Government service on or after 01.04.2025.

facts.fact: New recruits must opt within 30 days of joining
facts.quote: New recruits: Within 30 days of joining

facts.fact: Retired NPS subscribers who retired on or before 31.03.2025 can opt with at least 10 years of qualifying service or retirement under FR 56(j) (not as a penalty); the legally wedded spouse if the retiree has died
facts.quote: Retired NPS Subscribers who superannuated or retired on or before 31.03.2025, provided: Minimum 10 years of qualifying service. Retirement under FR 56(j) (not as a penalty). Legally wedded spouse as on date of retirement, in case of subscriber’s demise.

facts.fact: Past retirees get UPS benefits with arrears and interest at PPF rates
facts.quote: Past Retirees: Eligible for UPS benefits with arrears and interest (PPF rates).

facts.fact: The last date for existing employees and past retirees to opt for UPS was 30.11.2025
facts.quote: Note: The last date for eligible employees and past retirees under NPS to opt for UPS is 30.11.2025.
facts.note: The expected answer's check 'no further extension as of 15 Oct 2026' was repeated on 28 Oct 2026: no later extension found on PIB, PFRDA, NPS Trust or DFS; the PFRDA and NPS Trust UPS pages still say 'by 30th November 2025, or within such extended timelines if any'.

facts.fact: The deadline was first 30.06.2025, then extended by three months to 30.09.2025
facts.quote: the Government of India has decided to extend the cut-off date for exercising the option for UPS by three months i.e., upto 30 th September 2025 for eligible existing employees, past retirees, and the legally wedded spouses of deceased past retirees

facts.fact: It was then extended by two months to 30 November 2025 (PFRDA circular of 06.10.2025)
facts.quote: Extension of cut-off date for exercising Option of Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) under NPS by two months i.e., upto 30th November 2025 PDF ( 105 KB ) Published on: 06-10-2025

facts.fact: Anyone who does not opt stays in NPS
facts.quote: Default Applicability: If no option is exercised, the employee continues under NPS.

facts.fact: UPS has a one-time, one-way switch back to NPS
facts.quote: “One-time, one-way switch” option for reverting to the NPS.

summary: All UPS facts confirmed on NPS Trust pages, PIB (24.01.2025 notification, 02.09.2025 rules, deadline 30.06 -> 30.09 -> 30.11.2025) and the PFRDA circular of 06.10.2025; no later reopening found as of 28 Oct 2026.
